Nekrasove Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Nekrasove — known as Salishy when first mentioned in 1431, then Yuzvin from 1758, and its current name only since 1946 — was a genuinely mixed Ukrainian-Polish-Jewish town by the 1880s, with a population that included a synagogue alongside Orthodox and Catholic churches. On March 2, 1942, all 97 Jews still remaining in the town were shot to death. This cemetery, which received its most recent burial that same fateful year, was demolished in 1954, and part of the site was later converted into a sand pit during highway construction in 1980 — a fate shared with several other cemeteries in this collection.
